comment: pgrep self-match: a pgrep -f or pkill -f whose literal pattern matches the command's own text, so it finds every agent shell running a command with the same text, such as an earlier wait loop (must deny, naming the pattern), and forms that do not (must allow). The first deny case is the 2026-11-04 wait-loop shape verbatim.

deny.name: 2026-11-04 replay: wait loop on a lane check
deny.command: until ! pgrep -f "lane check X" >/dev/null; do sleep 15; done

deny.name: while loop, then a step after it
deny.command: while pgrep -f 'tools/lane land 597-x' > /dev/null; do sleep 30; done; echo landed

deny.name: as an if condition
deny.command: if pgrep -f lane-check >/dev/null; then echo busy; fi

deny.name: a regular expression that matches its own text

allow.name: one character bracketed
allow.command: until ! pgrep -f "[l]ane check X" >/dev/null; do sleep 15; done

allow.name: pattern in a variable from another command
allow.command: P=$(cat /tmp/pattern); until ! pgrep -f "$P" >/dev/null; do sleep 15; done

allow.name: plain pgrep without -f matches names only
allow.command: until ! pgrep vite >/dev/null; do sleep 5; done

allow.name: anchored at the start of the command line
allow.command: for i in $(seq 1 200); do pgrep -f '^python3 tools/lane land' >/dev/null || break; sleep 15; done

allow.name: a regular expression that does not match its own text
